content: # Comment Out HTML and PHP Together Attempting to comment out a block of mixed HTML and PHP code often leads to frustration when standard HTML comments fail to suppress the logic you intend to disable. The core issue lies in how the server interprets these syntaxes before they ever reach the browser. When you wrap a section containing `` tags inside an HTML comment ``, the server parses the file sequentially. It encounters the opening PHP tag, processes the code within it as executable logic, and then hits the closing PHP tag. Only after that does it encounter the HTML comment delimiters. Because the PHP engine has already executed the code, the surrounding HTML comment markers are effectively ignored by the interpreter, rendering your attempt to silence the block futile. To achieve a true "one-shot" comment for mixed environments, you must utilize the language-specific comment syntax that covers both languages simultaneously. PHP provides a multiline comment construct known as "nowdoc" style comments or simply using `` wrappers, but the most robust method for legacy codebases involves wrapping the entire block in PHP's own multi-line comment tags. The correct approach is to open with ``. This forces the PHP parser to treat everything between those markers as a string literal that is never executed, regardless of whether it contains HTML tags or other PHP logic.
